title: Update on lactose malabsorption and intolerance: pathogenesis, diagnosis and clinical management
authors: Misselwitz B, Butter M, Verbeke K, Fox MR
funder: The authors have not declared a specific grant for this research from any funding agency in the public, commercial or not-for-profit sectors.
authorConflicts: MF has received research funding from Nestlé International for studies of lactose digestion and tolerance.
result: Narrative review, commissioned. In lactose malabsorption, colonic bacteria ferment lactose to hydrogen, carbon dioxide, methane and short-chain fatty acids; the osmotic load in the colon rises about eightfold. Lactase persistence in Europeans is mediated by LCT-13910 C>T within intron 13 of MCM6, 13.9 kb upstream of LCT. Cow's milk contains about 5 g lactose per 100 mL; yoghurt contains about 50% of the lactose of unprocessed milk, and cheese has low lactose content, especially long-ripened cheese. Lactose-free dairy products are made by adding lactase to milk.
